services.name: Residential
services.short: Soft washing, pressure washing, and window cleaning for homes across the Lowcountry.
services.long: From historic Charleston single houses to new construction in Mount Pleasant, we tailor pressure and chemistry to protect your siding, paint, brick, and landscaping - while lifting years of grime, algae, and salt spray in a single visit.

services.name: Commercial
services.short: Storefronts, restaurants, offices, and parking lots - fully insured, flexibly scheduled.
services.long: Flexible scheduling including after-hours and early mornings so your customers only see the result. Fully insured, W-9 ready, and comfortable working around active operations from King Street boutiques to industrial facilities.

services.name: Docks
services.short: Marine-safe treatments, mildew and algae removal, and gentle wood restoration.
services.long: Charleston is a waterfront town, and your dock takes a beating. We use marine-safe chemistry to lift mildew, algae, and salt buildup and restore wood without harming the water around it.

locations.name: Mount Pleasant

locations.name: James Island
locations.short: Marsh-front homes and docks between the Stono and the harbor - soft washing and marine-safe dock care.
locations.long: James Island's marsh-front homes and docks take a beating from humidity, algae, and pluff mud spray. We bring soft-wash chemistry safe for landscaping and waterways, and marine-safe treatments for docks along the Stono River and the creeks feeding Charleston Harbor.

locations.name: West Ashley
locations.short: Established neighborhoods and busy retail corridors along Savannah Highway and Ashley River Road.
locations.long: West Ashley's mix of established neighborhoods and commercial corridors along Savannah Highway and Ashley River Road means we're just as comfortable soft washing a family home as we are scheduling after-hours pressure washing for a storefront or office.

locations.name: Daniel Island

locations.long: Daniel Island's newer homes and tight HOA standards call for clean, even results every time - soft-washed siding and roofs, pressure-washed driveways and pool decks, and marine-safe care for docks along the Cooper and Wando Rivers.

faqs.q: What's the difference between soft washing and pressure washing?
faqs.a: Soft washing uses low pressure and a cleaning solution to safely lift algae, mildew, and grime from siding and roofs without damaging paint or shingles. Pressure washing uses higher water pressure and is best suited for hard, durable surfaces like concrete driveways, pavers, and brick.

faqs.q: How often should I have my house washed?
faqs.a: Most Charleston homes benefit from an annual soft wash - the humidity and salt air here speed up algae and mildew growth. Homes in shaded or marsh-adjacent areas may need it more often.

faqs.q: Is soft washing safe for my landscaping and paint?
faqs.a: Yes. We use low-pressure application and rinse thoroughly, and we take care to protect plants and landscaping around your home during the process.

We serve homes across the Charleston peninsula and the greater Lowcountry, including Mount Pleasant, James Island, West Ashley, and Daniel Island. See our service area pages or reach out and we'll confirm.

faqs.q: Can you schedule around our business hours?
faqs.a: Yes - we regularly schedule early mornings, evenings, and weekends so cleaning doesn't interrupt your customers or operations.

faqs.q: Are you insured for commercial properties?
faqs.a: Yes, we're fully insured and can provide a W-9 and certificate of insurance for property managers and businesses that require it.

faqs.q: What kinds of commercial properties do you clean?
faqs.a: Storefronts, restaurants, offices, parking lots, sidewalks, and multi-tenant buildings across Charleston and the Lowcountry - from King Street boutiques to industrial facilities.

faqs.q: Do you offer recurring maintenance plans?
faqs.a: Many of our commercial clients book us on a recurring schedule to keep storefronts and walkways consistently clean. Ask about a maintenance plan when you request your quote.

bullets: No harm to marsh or waterway

faqs.q: Is your dock cleaning process safe for the marsh and waterway?
faqs.a: Yes - we use marine-safe chemistry specifically chosen to lift mildew, algae, and salt buildup without harming the marsh, pluff mud, or water around your dock.

faqs.q: Can you restore weathered or graying dock wood?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Our cleaning process lifts years of algae and salt buildup and can significantly brighten weathered wood, restoring a lot of its original look.

faqs.q: Do you clean boat lifts and boardwalks too?
faqs.a: Yes - we clean boardwalks, boat lifts, and dock decking as part of a full dock service.

faqs.q: How often does a dock need to be cleaned?
faqs.a: Most Lowcountry docks benefit from cleaning once or twice a year, depending on sun exposure and how close they sit to the marsh.

faqs.q: How high can the cleaning drone reach?
faqs.a: Our LucidBots drone system reaches 100+ feet, covering steeples, multi-story homes, and tall commercial facades that ladders and lifts can't safely reach.

faqs.q: Is drone cleaning safe for my property?
faqs.a: Yes - the drone applies the same low-pressure soft-wash chemistry we use on the ground, just from the air, so there's no ladder risk and no foot traffic on delicate roofing.

faqs.q: What kinds of buildings is drone cleaning best for?
faqs.a: Steeples, church facades, multi-story homes, condo and apartment buildings, and tall commercial exteriors where traditional access equipment is impractical or costly.

faqs.q: Do I need to be present during a drone cleaning?
faqs.a: No, but we do coordinate access and scheduling ahead of time. Reach out and we'll walk you through what to expect for your specific building.

team.heroSub: Locally owned, Charleston-based, and small on purpose. Two guys who show up, work hard, and treat your property like their own.

bio: Ben is the engineer of the group (Clemson class of 2024). But before college and all the way through it, he was working in the service industry.
Eight years of experience will teach you that the technical fix is only half the job - the other half is the person standing in front of you.
Off the clock, you'll find Ben on the golf course, on the mat, or enjoying live music at Chico Feo.
Nate is one of five kids. He grew up on a horse farm in Maryland - his family means everything to him.

Nate played college lacrosse for Bill Tierney at the University of Denver. His older brother Henry played at Notre Dame and his little brother Ben plays for Ohio State. Cousins scattered across Duke, Princeton, Maryland, Georgetown, Navy, Lehigh, Towson, Dartmouth, and High Point.
Nate enjoys competing in Brazilian jiu-jitsu and surfing/skating in his free time.
